messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High GPU request queue for customer-omega in private-vpc-us-west-2 — queue length 420, 95th latency > 12s, triggering paged on-call. Pager: @oncall-alex :rotating_light:
oncall-alex: acked. pulling logs now. seeing a sustained queue growth after 09:42 UTC.
eng-ml-sam: adding context — customer-omega uses dedicated private cluster (vpc-omega) with nodepool-gpu-rt, autoscaler ON but we recently bumped per-customer limit to 30 GPUs. they hit it?
sre-maya: checking autoscaler events. running kubectl get pods -A | grep Pending to see backlog.
infra-jordan: also checking cloud provider: listing recent scale requests.
oncall-alex: paste of kubectl events: ```
NAMESPACE   NAME                                  STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   
ml          gpu-infer-omega-0                     Pending   0          2m   
Events:  Type    Reason             Age   From               Message
  Normal  Scheduled          2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/gpu-infer-omega-0 to <none>
  Warning FailedScheduling    2m    default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: Insufficient GPUs.
```
eng-ml-sam: looks like pods are pending for GPU. but autoscaler should spin nodes. check CA logs.
infra-jordan: autoscaler log excerpt: ```
I0315 09:43:12 autoscaler.go:543] ScaleUp: need 4 nodes for pending 12 pods
I0315 09:43:13 cloudprovider.go:88] Requesting 4 instances in subnet subnet-omega-1
E0315 09:43:20 cloudprovider.go:123] Provision failed: QuotaExceeded: available IPv4 addresses in subnet-omega-1: 0
E0315 09:43:20 autoscaler.go:560] ScaleUp failed: insufficient IP addresses in subnet
```
oncall-alex: aha. subnet IP exhaustion in customer's private VPC. that explains no new nodes.
sre-maya: customer has hard limit on subnet size (they picked /28 earlier for private pools). we should confirm with customer-ops-rita. @customer-ops-rita can you confirm if they changed subnet sizing?
customer-ops-rita: confirming with customer — they say they recently encoded IP constraints for security. they expected us to fall back to burst region but we need explicit permission to create nodes in secondary subnet.
eng-ml-sam: impact note: customer requests are queuing -> API 429/503 for some calls? any error spikes?
oncall-alex: checking router logs: spike in 503s at 09:44 for /v1/generate for tenant omega ~25% error rate for 6 minutes. linked to queue saturation.
infra-jordan: can we route some traffic to hosted fallbacks? we have fallback model pool in hosted-east with same model version but customers on private mode opt-in for fallback. need customer's consent for failover.
oncall-alex: attempted scale with burst flag false -> stopped. we can manually create nodes in on-prem if customer allows, or request them to expand subnet.
sre-maya: mitigation options (ranked):
1) Ask customer to expand subnet size or free IPs (fastest if they can immediately).
2) Manual node registration into cluster using static IPs from customer admin — needs ops window.
3) Route low-priority inference to hosted fallback (requires ticket + consent).
4) Throttle new requests at edge for this tenant to preserve healthy pods.
eng-ml-sam: for (4) we can apply a temporary rate-limit rule per-tenant in edge gateway. that will reduce queue and keep SLO for higher-priority requests.
oncall-alex: executing temp throttling now: ```bash
# apply tenant throttle
redwoodctl gateway update-rate-limit --tenant omega --rps 5 --reason "mitigate subnet exhaustion"
```
oncall-alex: applied. queue dropped from 420 -> 160 in 3m. 503 rate down to 8%. :thumbsup:
customer-ops-rita: customer replied — can open a quick subnet change but need to coordinate with their network admin, ETA ~45m. they gave permission to enable hosted fallback for low-priority traffic.
eng-ml-sam: ok enabling fallback routing for low-priority models. updating routing policy.
deploy-bot: ROUTE CHANGE: traffic-policy/omega updated: low-priority -> hosted-east-fallback (effective 09:52 UTC).
eng-ml-sam: after fallback enabled, low-priority queue drained to ~30, high-priority still queued ~20 waiting for GPUs.
sre-maya: re-check autoscaler: it still can't provision because subnet IPs = 0. manual intervention needed if we want to add nodes earlier.
infra-jordan: we can also propose to the customer to move nodepool to secondary subnet (they have one unused /26) — requires credentials and an infra runbook step. how long to do manual node create? ~25-40m.
oncall-alex: customer network admin is in the thread: @customer-net-admin says they can free ~10 IPs immediately by deallocating old ENIs. doing now.
customer-net-admin: freed 12 IPs from dev ENIs. please retry scale.
infra-jordan: re-triggering autoscaler by annotating pending pods to re-evaluate: ```bash
kubectl annotate pod gpu-infer-omega-0 redwood/retry-scale=true --overwrite
```
infra-jordan: cloud logs: scale request accepted, provisioning 2 nodes, expected 6-8min.
oncall-alex: monitoring queue — dropping further. customer impact reduced. sending incident notification to customer success and account team.
sre-maya: summary for pager: root cause = subnet IP exhaustion in customer private VPC prevented autoscaler from provisioning nodes. contributing factors = small subnet (/28) for production nodepool and no automated fallback allowed by customer config. mitigation = edge throttling + hosted fallback enabled + customer freed IPs + manual retry.
eng-ml-sam: action items:
- infra to add autoscaler detection for subnet-IP-exhaustion and automatically surface clear remediation steps in console (infra-jordan).
- product: add opt-in 'auto-fallback' toggle in private settings with clear customer consent flow (eng-ml-sam).
- on-call: draft post-incident note and timeline (oncall-alex).
sre-maya: preparing handoff to night team. oncall-alex, any follow-ups?
oncall-alex: handoff: I'm switching to monitoring-only, handing oncall to @sre-maya for next 12h. logging runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/subnet-ip-exhaustion.
sre-maya: acked. waving off for now. will follow up if provisioning fails. :wave: 
customer-ops-rita: customer happy with mitigations, will schedule subnet resize for tomorrow with infra team. they requested a postmortem and potential SLA credit.
oncall-alex: noted. filing incident ticket INC-2212349999 and assigning to eng-ml-sam + infra-jordan for the postmortem.
sre-maya: last check 10:22 UTC — queues normalized, no active 503s for tenant omega. closing pager.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: High GPU queue for tenant omega — mitigation applied, root cause identified.
